cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: kube-controller-manager runs the built-in controllers, such as Deployment, ReplicaSet, Node and Job, inside one process. Each controller is a reconciliation loop scoped to one kind of resource that keeps actual state converging on desired state, without human action.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Each controller watches the API server, compares desired state (from etcd) with actual state, and corrects drift. Example: a ReplicaSet wants 3 Pods but 2 run, so the controller creates one. A Deployment owns ReplicaSets, which own Pods. It only talks to the API server, never to kubelets or etcd directly.

questions.q: Does kube-controller-manager talk to kubelets directly?
questions.a: No. It only reads and writes through the API server, never directly to a kubelet, worker node or etcd.
One watch-and-correct loop for one kind of resource that detects a mismatch between desired and actual state and acts to fix it.

questions.q: How do Deployments, ReplicaSets and Pods relate?
questions.a: A Deployment owns one or more ReplicaSets, and each ReplicaSet owns its Pods. The ReplicaSet controller keeps a fixed replica count running.
